LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 10.1.1 SIGNED PRESENTATIONS: DELIVERING SPEECHES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.1: Observing and Articulating Signs (Listening and Speaking) 10.1.1 Signed Presentations: Delivering Speeches
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating Signs (Listening and Speaking) 10.1.1 Signed Presentations: Delivering Speeches, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can one deliver a speech effectively?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating Signs (Listening and Speaking) 10.1.1 Signed Presentations: Delivering Speeches together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy : Learner develops interacting with technology skills as they use digital devices to record signed speeches as they

present them.

● Self-efficacy: Learner develop self-awareness and planning skills as they give attention to details while rehearsing speeches and

presenting them to each other in groups.

Values:
● Responsibility: is nurtured as learners care for digital devices as they record and present signed speeches

● Respect: is nurtured as learners respect each other’s work during discussions

Link to other Subjects

The learner is able to relate oral and signed presentations skills to their learning in Kiswahili or Kenya Sign Language
